column3: 4.1 Disposal of persons arrested under IPC Crimes by the Police. A total of 16,50,971 persons were under custody or on bail during investigation stage in 1975. This total included persons under arrest carried over from the previous year. The charge-sheets were laid for 78.0 per cent of the total persons under arrest and 11.5 per cent of the total remained under custody or on bail at the end of the year pending completion of investigation. The remaining 10.5 per cent of the total were released by the police or Magistrate before trial. The highest percentage of persons whose cases remained pending was under the crime head 'Counterfeiting' (30.7) followed by 'Criminal Breach of Trust' (27.7), 'Cheating' (24.6) and 'Dacority' (21.2). For the remaining crime heads, this percentage of pendency was below 20.0 but above 10.0 with the exception of the fees for which it was recorded as 9.2 per cent. The highest percentage in which charge-sheets could be laid to total number of persons under arrest was in respect of 'Thefts' (79.3) and the lowest percentage was under 'Dacority' (52.5). 4.3.1. Disposal of persons arrested under local and special Laws by the police.
A total of 37,57,990 persons including those carried over from the previous year were under custody during 1975 out of which charge-sheets could be laid against 89.4 per cent while investigations remained pending in respect of 9.7 per cent cases. The highest percentage in respect of those in whose cases investigaion could not be completed was under the 'Explosive and Explosive Substances Act' (31.3 per cent) and the lowest under the 'Indian Railways Act' (1.2 per cent). The relevant statistics are presented in Table 28. | 4.3.2. Disposal of persons arrested under the Local and special Laws by the courts.
A total of 44,45,947 persons were under trial during 1975 including those under trials carried over from the previous year. 27.3 per cent of the total under trials remained in custody at the end of the year and being completion of trial while 92.6 per cent of the total persons under trial to total persons in whose cases trials were completed were convicted during the year. The percentage of conviction to total persons whose trials were completed was consistently high and gene-rally above 75.0 per cent for most of the offences except 'Prevention of Corruption Act' for which it was recorded at 36.9 per cent.
